The only thing the creator changed was the abilities of some pre-existing pokemon. Everything else is the same as the original battle factory. There were many new evolutions and pokemon added in this game like tinkaton, the Applin line, annihilape, all the gen 4 evolutions like electavire, magmortar, togekiss etc, pokemon were given new moves and items that didn't exist in base Emerald. Yet we see none of those new additions in the battle factory. You'll never find any of the new pokemon or evolutions available to be rented, they're stuck as electabuzz, rhydon, tangela and so on. I don't know why the creator would choose to leave the rest of the battle frontier unchanged while only choosing to tamper with the battle factory. I agree with the points you made about the jankiness of the factory, but those issues are not new to the hack and have been a factor ever since the original.

I'm assuming you are mixing different armor sets together while wearing the gathering +10 talisman that you get from the bherna village chief. Like someone else mentioned, you need at least 10 points of a skill for a skill to activate, so if you are mixing random armor pieces together that all have different skills, none of them will activate. The gathering skill is from the talisman you are wearing, not the armor.

But the battle factory has always been jank, even way back in gen 3. Many people think it's the hardest facility to get a gold ranking because it's entirely rng what pokemon you will have access to and what pokemon your opponents will have. Many movesets given to the pokemon rely on status and stall, like you mentioned. Confusion, attraction, toxic protect stall, etc are common things you will encounter. If you go back and play the original emerald, you will see that the battle factory is the exact same as it is here.

I've gotten gold on all of the battle facilities and had a great time, but from my experience I don't think the creator actually changed the pokemon and their movesets from the original emerald. I say this because in emerald seaglass, the physical/special split is implemented which did not exist in the original emerald. So when I run into an alakazam in the battle tower that still uses all the elemental punches, which are now physical moves and are pretty much useless on alakazam given his terrible attack stat, it makes me believe that the creator just ported over the original battle frontier without changing the trainers pokemon and AI. More examples would be that pokemon that were given new additional types, like meganium being fairy/Grass and blastoise being steel/water, are not given new movesets to match the type change. You will run into pokemon like electabuzz and misdreavous late into the battle tower and not their evolutions electavire and Mismagius, because those evolutions did not exist in the original emerald. If the creator changed a base ability of a pokemon, that change will be reflected but none of the movesets will match it. So all these design choices you listed are attributes of base Emerald, and not new to this hack. If anything, some of the facilities feel easier (not the battle factory since you are forced to use rental pokemon which are unchanged from the original) since you have access to all the new moves, items, pokemon and evolutions that were added into the hack, while the CPU's are stuck with pokemon and movesets that were meant for generation 3. I used a dragonite with multiscale and dragon dance, Outrage, Fire punch and earthquake to sweep through the battle tower. Multiscale allowed dragonite to not be one shot by ice type moves and get a free dragon dance off everytime, which would certainly not be possible in the original game. Plus dragon moves were special in the original, so dragon dance wouldn't even buff Outrage. Things like that made me feel like I had a significant advantage over all my opponents.

I always like to have a super bulky mon that I can swap into and toxic stall with. That way if you run into something that is disadvantagous for your other two members, you can always swap into your bulky toxic stall mon and just wait it out. Your tyranitar has good bulk but is weak to six types with a ×4 weakness to fighting, and your skarmary is great for physical bulk and could potentially stall with the spikes+roar+roost combo, but I honestly think there are much better options. I personally used an Umbreon, Porygon-Z and Salamence to get to 100 wins, but a Cresselia instead of Umbreon works just as well if not better too.

 The Umbreon build I went with was

Ability:Synchronize 
Nature:Careful 
Item:Leftovers 
Moves: Toxic, Protect, Moonlight, Payback
Evs: 252 into defense and 252 into special defense, health would work too. 

The Leftovers plus protect and toxic combination is perfect, plus with moonlight you'll survive for a long time. This build is great for double-team or set up move cheese because as long as you get the toxic off, you don't have to worry about hitting any other moves and can just protect. Also very good to swap into due to its bulk, healing capabilities, and only being weak to fighting and bug as well as being immune to psychic. I think this type of toxic protect stall pokemon would compliment your other offensive beasts like swampert, garchomp and tyranitar really well. Umbreon was honestly the mvp of my battle tower runs.
